newsitem.title: FRANCE: Schneider accepts Spie buyout offer.
newsitem.headline: Schneider accepts Spie buyout offer.

text.p: French company Schneider said on Thursday it had accepted an offer by employees of its Spie Batignolles unit and British construction group Amec to buy out Spie Batignolles along with its holding in Spie-Trindel.

Schneider said in a statement the deal involves an offer of 350 million francs to buy 100 percent of Spie Batignolles and 400 million francs for the purchase of 31 percent of Spie-Trindel held directly by Schneider.

Spie Batignolles will promise to buy the remaining 19 percent held by Schneider in Spie-Trindel within three years. "In total the immediate and delayed elements of the transaction amount to one billion francs," Schneider said.
Up to now, Spie-Trindel was held 50-50 by Schneider and Spie Batignolles.
Spie Batignolles will be majority-owned by its employees. Some 60 percent will be owned by workers, said a person close to the operation.
Under the agreement, after six years, Amec will have the right to buy out all of Spie Batignolles shares, Schneider said.
